text: Keynes wrote the General Theory in 1936 to dislodge the classical assumption that labour markets clear on their own; aggregate demand became the organising variable and involuntary unemployment stopped being a definitional contradiction.

queries.text: which 1936 book broke with the classical self-clearing labour market and elevated aggregate demand
keynes general theory 1936 aggregate demand unemployment classical

text: Hicks distilled the General Theory into the IS-LM diagram in his 1937 Econometrica paper, giving the profession a tractable two-curve picture of output and interest determination that textbooks would lean on for decades.

queries.text: who formalised Keynes into the IS-LM apparatus and in which journal did it first appear
hicks is lm econometrica 1937 keynes diagram output interest

text: Samuelson's neoclassical synthesis stitched Keynesian short-run demand management onto the classical long-run equilibrium core; his Foundations of Economic Analysis supplied the maths and Economics made it pedagogy.

queries.text: whose synthesis glued Keynesian demand management onto a classical long-run core
samuelson neoclassical synthesis foundations economics keynes classical

text: Milton Friedman's monetarism argued that inflation is everywhere and always a monetary phenomenon; the permanent-income hypothesis and the k-percent rule followed as natural implications of that single primitive.

queries.text: which doctrine treats inflation as a purely monetary phenomenon and who championed it
friedman monetarism inflation money permanent income k percent rule

text: The Lucas critique demolished reduced-form policy evaluation by pointing out that agent decision rules shift when the policy rule shifts; any model fitted on one regime cannot be used to rank counterfactual regimes.

queries.text: which critique showed that reduced-form policy simulations collapse when the policy regime itself changes
lucas critique reduced form policy rule decision rule regime

text: Kydland and Prescott launched real business cycle theory with their 1982 Time to Build paper, insisting that a neoclassical growth model with technology shocks could replicate cyclical moments without nominal frictions.

queries.text: which 1982 paper kicked off real business cycle theory and who wrote it
kydland prescott rbc time to build 1982 technology shock cycle

text: Woodford's Interest and Prices reconstructed monetary theory without money: the central bank sets an interest rate, expectations about future rates pin down current inflation, and the quantity of base money becomes a passive residual.

queries.text: which Woodford treatise laid out monetary policy with interest as the instrument and money as a residual
woodford interest prices monetary central bank rate expectation

text: Gali's textbook on the New Keynesian framework codified the three-equation canonical model with sticky prices a la Calvo, a dynamic IS equation, and a forward-looking Phillips curve driven by real marginal cost.

queries.text: which textbook codified the canonical three-equation New Keynesian model and who wrote it
gali new keynesian three equation calvo sticky price phillips is

text: Bernanke and Gertler's financial accelerator added a credit channel to New Keynesian DSGE: agency costs make external finance premia countercyclical, so balance-sheet shocks amplify and propagate small disturbances.

queries.text: which mechanism lets balance-sheet frictions amplify shocks inside a DSGE model and who formalised it
bernanke gertler financial accelerator credit channel dsge balance

text: The campus vending machine ate another dollar and the physics grad students taped a handwritten warning to the coin slot.

DSGE became the lingua franca of central-bank macro in the 2000s; Smets and Wouters estimated an extended New Keynesian model on euro-area data and showed it could beat Bayesian VARs at forecasting horizons out to a year.

queries.text: which estimated DSGE model beat Bayesian VAR forecasts on euro-area data in the 2000s
dsge smets wouters bayesian var euro area forecast new keynesian

text: The Ramsey-Cass-Koopmans model closes the Solow setup by letting households pick consumption to maximise a discounted utility integral; the Euler equation and transversality condition jointly determine the saving rate endogenously.

queries.text: which growth model endogenises the saving rate by optimising household utility and how
ramsey cass koopmans solow euler transversality saving rate utility

text: Solow's 1956 growth paper showed that capital accumulation alone cannot sustain per-capita growth; exogenous technological progress has to do the heavy lifting once the economy reaches its steady state.

queries.text: which 1956 paper showed capital accumulation alone cannot drive long-run per-capita growth
solow 1956 growth steady state technology exogenous capital

text: Romer's 1990 endogenous growth paper modelled ideas as non-rival goods produced by an R&D sector; increasing returns at the aggregate level let technology be an outcome of incentives rather than a free gift.

queries.text: which 1990 paper modelled technological progress as the output of a profit-motivated R&D sector
romer endogenous growth 1990 r and d non rival ideas technology

text: Lucas's 1988 Mechanics of Economic Development paper used human capital externalities rather than R&D to drive endogenous growth; the same idea animated his later work on city-level spillovers and cross-country income gaps.

queries.text: which 1988 Lucas paper routed endogenous growth through human capital externalities
lucas 1988 mechanics human capital externality endogenous growth

text: The original Phillips curve was an empirical regularity on UK wage inflation against unemployment from 1861 to 1957; the theoretical reinterpretation as a menu for policy came later and did not survive the 1970s.

queries.text: which data span did Phillips originally fit and what went wrong when policy treated it as a menu
phillips curve 1861 1957 uk wage inflation unemployment menu 1970

text: Friedman and Phelps argued the Phillips curve trade-off holds only for unexpected inflation; NAIRU emerged as the long-run rate where expectations catch up and the curve becomes vertical at the natural rate of unemployment.

queries.text: whose argument made the long-run Phillips curve vertical and introduced the NAIRU
friedman phelps nairu natural rate phillips vertical expectation

text: The Taylor rule that Stanford's John Taylor proposed in 1993 set the federal funds rate as a linear response to inflation and output gaps with a coefficient above one on inflation; it fit US Fed behaviour remarkably well.

queries.text: which 1993 rule linked the federal funds rate to inflation and output gaps with a super-unitary inflation coefficient
taylor rule 1993 fed funds inflation output gap coefficient stanford

text: New Zealand adopted formal inflation targeting in 1990 under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act; the UK, Canada, and Sweden followed, and the regime became the default operating framework for inflation-averse central banks.

entities.name: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act

queries.text: which country first adopted formal inflation targeting and under which act did it take effect
inflation targeting new zealand 1990 rbnz uk canada sweden regime

text: Sims's 1980 Macroeconomics and Reality paper pushed the profession toward VAR analysis; identifying shocks through Choleski ordering or later long-run restrictions sidestepped the incredible identifying assumptions of structural models.

queries.text: which 1980 Sims paper made VAR analysis the default alternative to structural macro models
sims 1980 macroeconomics reality var choleski shock identification

text: FAVAR methods by Bernanke, Boivin, and Eliasz extended the standard VAR with factors extracted from hundreds of time series; the larger information set cured the price puzzle that haunted small recursive VARs.

queries.text: which factor-augmented VAR extension cured the price puzzle and who proposed it
favar bernanke boivin eliasz factor var price puzzle information

text: Bernanke and Blinder's 1988 paper on the credit channel pointed at bank-loan supply as a second transmission route for monetary policy beyond the standard interest-rate channel, especially in bank-dependent sectors.

queries.text: which 1988 paper identified a bank-lending credit channel alongside the interest-rate channel
bernanke blinder credit channel 1988 bank loan monetary transmission

text: Reinhart and Rogoff's This Time Is Different compiled eight centuries of debt, default, and inflation episodes; the follow-up Growth in a Time of Debt claimed a 90 percent public-debt threshold, which a later spreadsheet error partially walked back.

entities.name: Growth in a Time of Debt

queries.text: which Reinhart Rogoff pair of works proposed the 90 percent debt threshold and what undermined it
reinhart rogoff this time different growth debt 90 percent spreadsheet

text: Piketty's Capital in the Twenty-First Century argued that when r exceeds g for prolonged periods, the capital share and top wealth shares grow mechanically; the WTID database behind the claims made the empirics auditable.

queries.text: which Piketty book built its inequality thesis on r exceeds g and an auditable database
piketty capital twenty first century wtid r g wealth share

text: Blanchard served as IMF chief economist during the 2008 crisis and spent years coaxing the profession toward fiscal multiplier estimates well above one in downturns, reversing the pre-crisis near-consensus on small multipliers.

queries.text: which IMF chief economist pushed large downturn fiscal multipliers after the 2008 crisis
blanchard imf chief economist fiscal multiplier 2008 crisis

text: Mankiw's undergraduate Macroeconomics textbook became the default intermediate course text in the United States; successive editions tracked the profession's drift from IS-LM as centrepiece to three-equation New Keynesian teaching modules.

queries.text: which Mankiw textbook's successive editions migrated US intermediate courses from IS-LM to New Keynesian teaching
mankiw macroeconomics textbook intermediate is lm new keynesian us

text: Acemoglu's Introduction to Modern Economic Growth is a graduate-level brick; it covers Solow, Ramsey-Cass-Koopmans, overlapping generations, endogenous growth, directed technical change, and political-economy models of long-run development in one volume.

queries.text: which Acemoglu graduate text covers Solow through directed technical change and political-economy growth in one volume
acemoglu introduction modern economic growth graduate solow overlapping

text: Stiglitz's public economics work on information asymmetries reshaped the microfoundations macroeconomists were willing to admit; adverse selection and moral hazard became respectable building blocks in models of credit rationing and unemployment.

queries.text: whose information-asymmetry work put adverse selection and moral hazard into serious macro models
stiglitz public economics asymmetric information adverse selection moral

text: The zero lower bound on nominal interest rates became the binding constraint for the US Fed, the ECB, and the Bank of Japan after 2008; forward guidance and quantitative easing filled in for rate cuts that could not happen.

queries.text: which post-2008 constraint forced central banks to rely on forward guidance and quantitative easing
zero lower bound fed ecb boj 2008 forward guidance qe rate

text: Modigliani's life-cycle hypothesis and Friedman's permanent-income hypothesis both argued consumption tracks expected lifetime resources rather than current income; the implications for fiscal multipliers are profound and still contested.

queries.text: which two hypotheses argued consumption tracks lifetime resources and why it matters for fiscal multipliers
modigliani life cycle friedman permanent income consumption fiscal

text: Kydland and Prescott's 1977 time-inconsistency paper showed that discretion without commitment yields a systematic inflation bias; the result became the canonical argument for independent central banks bound by explicit mandates.

queries.text: which 1977 Kydland-Prescott result motivated independent central banks with explicit mandates
kydland prescott 1977 time inconsistency inflation bias commitment

text: Calvo pricing, proposed by Guillermo Calvo, assumes a random fraction of firms reset prices each period; the resulting aggregate-supply curve has a forward-looking term in expected inflation plus a current marginal cost driver, which became the backbone of New Keynesian DSGE.

queries.text: which price-setting assumption drives the New Keynesian Phillips curve and who authored it
calvo pricing random reset forward inflation marginal cost nk dsge

text: Sargent and Wallace's unpleasant monetarist arithmetic showed that if the fiscal authority runs persistent deficits, the monetary authority eventually has to monetise them; central-bank independence alone cannot guarantee price stability.

queries.text: which Sargent-Wallace result shows fiscal deficits can swamp central-bank independence
sargent wallace unpleasant monetarist arithmetic fiscal monetise

text: The rational expectations hypothesis, formalised by Muth in 1961 and weaponised by Lucas in the 1970s, replaced adaptive expectations in serious macro; forecasts now had to be consistent with the model the modeller was running.

queries.text: which expectations formalism did Lucas use to displace adaptive expectations and who first proposed it
rational expectations muth 1961 lucas adaptive macro forecast

text: Diamond-Mortensen-Pissarides search-and-matching theory explained equilibrium unemployment as the output of a matching function with vacancies and unemployed workers; the 2010 Nobel went to that framework.

queries.text: which 2010 Nobel framework explained equilibrium unemployment through a matching function
diamond mortensen pissarides search matching unemployment nobel 2010

text: Eggertsson and Krugman revived the liquidity trap in a New Keynesian setting with borrowing constraints; at the zero lower bound, deleveraging shocks make even standard multipliers bigger and paradox of thrift results return.

queries.text: which New Keynesian revival of the liquidity trap brought back the paradox of thrift at the zero lower bound
eggertsson krugman liquidity trap nk zlb paradox thrift multiplier

text: Okun's law is an empirical rule of thumb that a one-point rise in unemployment tracks about a two-point fall in output growth relative to potential; it holds up reasonably in US data but wobbles across countries and decades.

queries.text: which empirical rule links unemployment changes to output-growth gaps and where does it hold best
okun law unemployment output gap growth us decade country

text: The Fisher equation nominal equals real plus expected inflation is the closure device that lets the Taylor rule pin down real rates; without it, changes in the nominal policy rate cannot be mapped to aggregate demand effects.

queries.text: which identity bridges nominal and real rates so the Taylor rule can move aggregate demand
fisher equation nominal real expected inflation taylor rule demand

text: Barro's 1974 Ricardian equivalence argument showed that with infinite-horizon altruistic households, debt-financed tax cuts are saved rather than spent; dynasties internalise the future tax liability and current consumption does not move.

queries.text: which 1974 Barro argument claims debt-financed tax cuts get saved rather than spent
barro 1974 ricardian equivalence tax cut debt consumption dynasty

text: The Blanchard-Kahn 1980 paper gave rational expectations modellers the solvability conditions for linear models with forward-looking variables; the count of unstable eigenvalues has to match the count of jump variables or no solution exists.

queries.text: which 1980 conditions tell rational-expectations modellers when a linear forward-looking system has a solution
blanchard kahn 1980 rational expectations eigenvalue jump variable

text: The neo-Fisherian puzzle observes that sustained low policy rates in Japan and the euro area did not raise inflation as standard New Keynesian models implied; Cochrane and others pushed a reinterpretation where raising rates raises inflation.

queries.text: which reinterpretation of the Fisher relation grew out of the failure of low rates to raise inflation in Japan and Europe
neo fisherian japan euro area cochrane nk low rate inflation

text: HANK models, which stands for Heterogeneous Agent New Keynesian and were built by Kaplan, Moll, and Violante, add idiosyncratic income risk and a distribution of balance sheets on top of the New Keynesian core; marginal propensities to consume vary sharply across households.

queries.text: which heterogeneous-agent extension of New Keynesian macro lets marginal propensities to consume differ across households
hank kaplan moll violante heterogeneous mpc new keynesian distribution

text: The library coffee cart is down to two kinds of pastry and the queue at 3 pm still wraps around the atrium.

The Great Moderation from 1984 through roughly 2007 saw US output and inflation volatility fall by half; whether better monetary policy or structural luck drove it remained a live debate right up until the 2008 crisis ended the moderation.

queries.text: which 1984 to 2007 period cut US macro volatility in half and what ended it
great moderation 1984 2007 us volatility monetary luck 2008

text: Reinhart, Reinhart, and Rogoff documented that post-crisis recovery paths systematically run below pre-crisis growth rates for roughly a decade; the paper shaped expectations about the slow US recovery after 2008.

queries.text: which post-crisis-recovery paper by Reinhart and Rogoff shaped expectations after 2008
reinhart rogoff post crisis recovery decade slow 2008 us

text: John Taylor himself preferred a rule-based monetary regime; he criticised the Fed's discretionary deviations from the simple Taylor rule during the 2003-2005 low-rate period as a contributor to the housing boom that preceded the 2008 crisis.

queries.text: whose rule-based preference blamed Fed deviations in 2003 to 2005 for the housing boom
taylor rule fed 2003 2005 deviation housing boom 2008 discretion

text: Piketty prefers progressive wealth taxation over income taxation as the lever against r exceeds g dynamics; the policy recommendation is controversial and the practical design questions around enforcement remain open.

queries.text: which tax instrument does Piketty prefer against r exceeds g dynamics
piketty wealth tax income progressive r g inequality enforcement

text: Friedman preferred rules over discretion; his proposed k-percent rule fixed money-supply growth regardless of current conditions, and the preference extended to floating exchange rates and a negative income tax.

queries.text: which three rule-based positions did Friedman consistently prefer over discretion
friedman rules discretion k percent float exchange negative income

text: Stiglitz preferred activist fiscal policy and heavier financial regulation to the Washington Consensus prescriptions he had helped articulate at the World Bank; the preference hardened after the East Asian crisis of 1997.

queries.text: whose post-1997 position flipped against the Washington Consensus toward fiscal activism
stiglitz washington consensus world bank east asian 1997 fiscal

text: The 2008 financial crisis terminated the Great Moderation narrative, triggered coordinated fiscal stimulus across the G20, and reopened debates on liquidity traps, financial frictions, and macroprudential regulation that had seemed settled.

queries.text: which 2008 event ended the Great Moderation and reopened debates on liquidity traps and macroprudential regulation
2008 financial crisis great moderation g20 liquidity trap macroprudential
